body:
Source: GitHub issue #992 (bug, area:autopilot). Re-verified on main @ c410918c.

THE DEFECT. `packages/autopilot/lib/run.mjs:143-146` — the catch around the worker mirror / worker deps build:

    } catch (e) {
      ctx.records.update(n, { lastError: `${e.code ?? 'init-failed'}: ${e.message}` });
      return { state: 'failed', reason: e.code ?? 'init-failed', exitCode: 1, detail: e.message, ticketId };
    }

`records.update` throws when the record is gone — `lib/records.mjs:70-72`: `const cur = load(issue); if (!cur) throw new Error(\`no run record for issue ${issue}\`);`. Because that throw happens INSIDE a catch block, it replaces the clean `{ state: 'failed', reason: 'init-failed' }` the code is trying to return and escapes as an unhandled rejection. The same file already guards this hazard in its two sibling sites, both of which return cleanly instead of throwing: `run.mjs:154-161` (the rounds loop, `if (!currentRecord) return { state: 'unchanged', reason: 'record-vanished', ticketId };`) and `run.mjs:171-176` (`resumeRun`, same shape). Both carry a `#962:` comment. The init-failure handler is the third site with the same hazard and did not get the guard.

OBSERVED. CI 2026-09-11, `test (22)` on PR #989 — a diff touching zero autopilot files. Run 34588776847, job 103229006399: `not ok 4 - AC121: every registered criterion names a mutation fixture that BITES`, `failureType: 'unhandledRejection'`, `error: 'no run record for issue 7'`, stack `Object.update (packages/autopilot/lib/records.mjs:71:21)` → `continueRun (packages/autopilot/lib/run.mjs:144:17)`. `test (18)` and `test (20)` passed on the identical commit. Note the misattribution: the rejection surfaced under AC121, which has nothing to do with the defect — that is the signature of a stale continuation escaping after its owning call ended.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/autopilot` (the local issue autopilot). Run its suite with `npm test -w packages/autopilot` from the worktree root; a single file with `node --test packages/autopilot/test/<f>.test.mjs`. Module map for the files that matter here: `lib/run.mjs` (continueRun/resumeRun — the per-issue state machine), `lib/records.mjs` (the run-record store; `update` THROWS on a missing record), `lib/deps.mjs` (cloneAt/buildWorkerDeps/installGateDeps), `lib/paths.mjs` (the run directory layout incl. `gateDeps`), `lib/mirror.mjs` (worker + gate mirrors), `lib/git-env.mjs` (gitBaseEnv / NET_GIT template — carries the #962 gc.auto precedent), `test/helpers/recover-fixture.mjs` and `test/helpers/sequence-fixture.mjs` (the two fixtures).

TEST-REGISTRY FACT you need before writing tests: `packages/autopilot/test/ac-registry.mjs` maps SPEC criterion numbers to test functions and `test/spec-coverage.test.mjs` enforces it. A regression test for a BUGFIX is NOT a spec criterion and MUST NOT be added to that registry — the precedent is the #962 fix (commit ca7299e5 / 763bd2a5), whose `ac962_…` tests are named after the ISSUE number and appear nowhere in `ac-registry.mjs`. Do not edit `ac-registry.mjs`, `test/spec-coverage.test.mjs`, or `docs/specs/issue-autopilot-local.md`.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. THE FIX IS AT THE CALL SITE, NOT IN THE STORE. `lib/records.mjs` is a rail. `records.update` must keep throwing on a missing record — that contract is load-bearing for every other caller, and turning it into a silent no-op would hide real bugs. Guard the CALL in `run.mjs`.
2. THE INIT-FAILURE RESULT SURVIVES THE MISSING RECORD. When the record has vanished, the handler must still return the failure it was built to return — `{ state: 'failed', reason: e.code ?? 'init-failed', exitCode: 1, detail: e.message, ticketId }` — NOT throw, and NOT substitute `{ state: 'unchanged', reason: 'record-vanished' }`. This differs deliberately from the two sibling sites: they are mid-flight checks where 'unchanged' is the truthful answer, whereas here the run HAS already failed and the caller must learn the reason. The record write is best-effort bookkeeping; the return value is the contract.
3. AUDIT EVERY OTHER `records.update` CALL SITE IN THE FILE and state the verdict for each in the PR body. They are at lines 41, 75, 79, 95, 127, 132 and 144. `:75` already guards with `if (record())`. For each of the others decide, with a reason, whether a vanished record there can (a) escape as an unhandled rejection, (b) replace a meaningful return value, or (c) is genuinely unreachable/harmless because a caller has already proven the record exists on that path. Fix the ones that are (a) or (b) under this same ticket; leave (c) alone and say why. Do not blanket-wrap every call in try/catch — a swallowed write that SHOULD have succeeded is a new defect, not a fix.
4. NO SWALLOWED ERRORS. Whatever guard you choose must distinguish "the record is gone" (tolerate, continue, return the real result) from "the write failed for some other reason" (must not be silently discarded). A bare `try {} catch {}` around the update fails this criterion.
4. Documentation: NONE. This change alters no user-facing CLI surface, flag, exit code or output, so `packages/autopilot/README.md` and `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/autopilot.mdx` are NOT to be edited. (`docs/tools/autopilot.md` does not exist for this package.) Explain the change in the PR body instead.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 With the mirror/deps build made to throw AND the run record removed before the catch runs, `continueRun` RESOLVES with `{ state: 'failed', reason: 'init-failed', exitCode: 1 }` carrying the thrown error’s detail and the ticketId — it does not reject, and no unhandled rejection is emitted. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run-init-failure.test.mjs`
- AC2 With the same build failure but the record PRESENT, the record is still updated with `lastError` = `‹code›: ‹message›` exactly as today, and the same failed result is returned — the guard does not cost the bookkeeping on the normal path. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run-init-failure.test.mjs`
- AC3 An update failure that is NOT a missing record still propagates rather than being swallowed. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run-init-failure.test.mjs`
- AC4 RED FIRST: AC1 fails against `lib/run.mjs` as it exists at origin/main, with `no run record for issue <n>` (not some unrelated error), and the test observes it as a REJECTION/unhandled rejection rather than a returned value. Record the exact red output in the PR body. verify: stash the `run.mjs` change and re-run `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run-init-failure.test.mjs`
- AC5 Every `records.update` site named in NORMATIVE 3 has a written verdict in the PR body, and any site classified (a) or (b) has a test in the same new file. verify: `grep -n "records.update" packages/autopilot/lib/run.mjs` and the PR body
- AC6 Existing suite green. verify: `npm test -w packages/autopilot`
- AC7 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: issue #990 (the nested gate-deps gc guard) and issue #994 (AC9’s bounded spin-wait) are being fixed in two sibling branches at the same time. Do not touch `packages/autopilot/test/helpers/recover-fixture.mjs`, `packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs`, `packages/autopilot/test/quota.test.mjs` or `packages/autopilot/test/helpers/sequence-fixture.mjs` — edits there will collide. #990 is a plausible TRIGGER for this defect (its clone failure is exactly what lands in this catch block) but fixing it would only make this rarer, not correct; do not wait on it or fold it in.
title: autopilot: give continueRun’s init-failure handler the vanished-record guard its two siblings already have
